heroLead: Slow, soothing 1:1 sessions of easy movement, calming breathwork, and deep rest — built around your body, your routine, and how you feel each day. Practised alongside the care your doctor provides.
empathyLabel: You don't have to do this alone
empathyText: Keeping calm matters when your blood pressure is high. Yoga can be one gentle, steadying thing you add to your week — never something that replaces what your doctor has you doing.
helpsH2: How yoga can support blood pressure.
helpsSubhead: Four gentle levers, working together — and the first one does most of the lifting.

levers.title: Calmer mind, calmer body
levers.body: Stress can push blood pressure up; slow breathing and relaxation help quiet that response and settle the nervous system.

levers.title: Gentle movement, no strain
levers.body: Easy, regular movement keeps you active without the strain or breath-holding that can spike pressure.

levers.title: Better sleep, steadier days
levers.body: Poor sleep makes blood pressure harder to manage; restful practice helps you wind down and rest more deeply.

levers.title: A habit you can keep
levers.body: Short, sustainable sessions you actually look forward to; consistency is what makes the difference over time.

posesH2: The poses we focus on, and why.
posesSubhead: Grouped by what they do for the body. Your teacher draws from these — they won't ask you to do all of them.

poseGroups.why: Easy mobility that keeps you active without strain.

poseGroups.note: We keep the head at or above heart level and leave out full inversions and any breath-holding — important when blood pressure is high.

poseGroups.why: Calming the stress response that can push pressure up.

poses.desc: Slow, even, and settling breath that quiets the nervous system.

A calming, cooling breath drawn in slowly to soothe.

poseGroups.why: Good rest supports calmer, steadier days.

A still close to every session, letting everything you've done settle in.
A quiet, settling seat to soften the mind and ease the day.

selectionNote: Your teacher won't hand you all of these. They'll choose the right few for your body, your level, and how you're feeling that day.
howH2: How we work with you to get there.
howSubhead: One teacher who knows your name and your goals — not a different face every week.

steps.title: We get to know you
steps.body: A relaxed first session: your diagnosis, what your doctor advises, your medication timing, your routine, and anything to work around like dizziness.

steps.title: A plan shaped to you
steps.body: Your teacher chooses the poses, pace, and breathing that suit you, keeping everything gentle.

steps.title: Guided live 1:1s
steps.body: The same teacher every time, on Google Meet, adjusting each session to how you feel.

steps.title: We grow it gently
steps.body: Small, steady progress and habits you can keep — always alongside your medical care.

faqs.q: Can yoga lower or replace my blood-pressure medication?
faqs.a: No. Yoga sits alongside the care your doctor provides — it isn't a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Never change or stop anything without speaking to your doctor first.

faqs.q: Are there poses I should avoid with high blood pressure?
faqs.a: Yes — full inversions, breath-holding, and forceful breathing can raise pressure, so your teacher leaves these out and keeps your head at or above heart level.

faqs.q: Do I need to be fit or flexible to start?
faqs.a: Not at all. Sessions begin wherever you are, with chair options and gentler variations whenever you need them.

faqs.q: What if my blood pressure isn't well controlled yet?
faqs.a: Please check with your doctor first, and tell your teacher — we'll keep everything especially gentle and calm.

faqs.q: How soon might I notice anything?
faqs.a: Everyone is different. Many people first notice they feel calmer and sleep better. Please track your readings with your doctor, not with us.

safetyTitle: Yoga supports your care — it doesn't replace it
safetyText: These sessions support your overall wellbeing and are practised alongside professional medical care. They are not a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Please tell your teacher about any conditions or symptoms so they can adapt your session safely, and keep your doctor in the loop.
metaDescription: Gentle 1:1 yoga for high blood pressure — slow movement, calming breathwork, and deep rest that may support relaxation and steadier, calmer days, practised alongside your medical care. First session free.
